messages:
anya: Heads up -- rolling FlashAttention v3 to a small subset of prod pods right now. Observing a p95 token latency bump ~+12% on short sequences (12-64 tokens). Canary didn't show this. Need quick triage.
kevin: What are the exact workload shapes? sampling vs greedy? batch sizes? any difference between canary and live traffic? :thinking_face:
sara: Do we have kernel_choice telemetry emitted? need chosen kernel + effective_seqlen + pad_ratio to correlate.
matt: Peeked at a couple traces. FlashV3 often picks an FMHA variant that requires a larger workspace for some shapes. That seems to trigger allocator contention on live nodes. Likely workspace allocation/fragmentation issue.
dmitri: Is this BF16/FP16 specific? we've seen allocator behavior differ when using bf16 pools vs cudaMalloc directly.
anya: It's bf16 on these pods. Traffic is sampling (temp=0.8), median output ~24 tokens. Canary used same binary/config but different traffic composition (more long chat streams). Live has many tiny requests.
sara: If many tiny requests get padded up (we pad batches to nearest 16), the effective seqlen can flip kernel heuristics. Can we log effective seqlen?
matt: I grabbed kernel selection logs from one affected pod: it chose `flashv3-block64` which needs ~60MB extra workspace per request for that shape. When concurrent requests hit, allocator latency increases. Hypothesis: flashv3's workspace rounding + pool policy -> more churn.
anya: Config snippet for selector we're using: ```
kernel_selector:
  prefer_flashv3: true
  fallback_order: [flashv3, flashv2, triton_fmha]
  workspace_pool: auto
  workspace_hard_limit: null
```
kevin: Try workspace_pool: static with a small per-worker reservation (e.g. 256MB) and set workspace_hard_limit so we don't do per-request cudaMallocs. Also consider rounding workspaces to 128-byte multiples to reduce fragmentation.
sara: Another angle: pad_ratio. If tokenization pads from 7 to 16 often, that >2x pad ratio will move shapes into a different kernel bucket. We should tag requests with pad_ratio and chosen_kernel.
dmitri: I'm rolling a synthetic microbench to replay sampled seqlen distro + batching scheme from live traffic to reproduce. Will test with: batching strategy = continuous_batching and pad_to_multiple = 16.
anya: Action items: 1) dmitri run replay job; 2) kevin try static pool + workspace rounding on a staging subset; 3) sara add kernel_choice telemetry (chosen_kernel + effective_seqlen + pad_ratio). I'll pause rollout until we have data.
deploy-bot: Rolling stop initiated by anya at 2067890180. Canary unaffected.
kevin: If static pool + rounding fixes the latency, we can add a simple selector heuristic: if effective_seqlen <= 32 AND pad_ratio > 1.25 then prefer flashv2 (or flashv3 with tight workspace). That avoids blind global toggles.
sara: +1. I'll add a small dashboard tile: pad_ratio vs p95 latency by kernel. Also wire an alert if p95 jumps >8% for short-seq bucket.
matt: Also keep an eye on KV cache warmstart. I saw a small extra allocation on first token after cache warmup for flashv3; ensure that temporary KV workspace is reused.
anya: Good catch. Please gather perf counters if you can: sm_efficiency, l2_bandwidth, allocator-time. Drop them here if you reproduce.
dmitri: Started job 2067890300 (replay). ETA ~25-35m, will post summarized diffs.
kevin: One more config we can toggle quickly: prefer_flashv3 -> conditional_on_pad_ratio <= 1.25. We can roll that as a per-route override for high-QPS short-seq routes.
sara: I'll add REDWOOD_ATTENTION_DEBUG sampling flag to capture kernel metadata for ~0.1% of requests so we can triangulate without heavy overhead.
anya: Thanks all. If someone gets a repro trace, paste the full trace snippet (call stacks + chosen_kernel) here. We'll reconvene after dmitri posts the replay results. :thumbsup:
